title: PGs & Hostels in Bengaluru: Addresses & Phone Numbers
metaDescription: 20 pgs & hostels in Bengaluru with addresses and phone numbers, plus what to check before you visit.
intro: Bengaluru's rental market moves fast, and PGs and hostels can range from spotless shared spaces to cramped, poorly maintained rooms. Whether you're a student, young professional, or newcomer to the city, visiting in person and asking the right questions makes all the difference. This guide walks you through what to check, what to confirm, and how to avoid common mistakes.

sections.heading: Start by Listing Your Real Priorities
sections.body: Before you visit anywhere, write down what actually matters to you. Is proximity to your college or office non-negotiable, or are you flexible on location if the room is cheaper or nicer? Do you need a dedicated desk, or is a bed enough? Will you cook, or do you need tiffin or meal options included? Can you live with shared bathrooms, or do you need your own? Some people prioritize natural light and windows; others care most about internet speed and study space. Knowing this upfront saves you time visiting places that won't work anyway. Once you've listed your top 3–4 must-haves and your nice-to-haves, you'll recognize a good fit when you see it.

sections.heading: What to Inspect When You Visit
sections.body: Visit during the time you'll actually be there — if you sleep at 10 p.m., visit in the evening. Check water pressure and temperature in the bathroom, flush the toilet, look for leaks under the sink and around pipes. Open windows and smell the room — dampness, mold, or musty odors are real problems that photos hide. Look at the bed mattress closely; press it, check for stains or sagging. Count electrical outlets near where you'll study or charge devices. Ask to see the kitchen if meals aren't provided, and check if it's clean and has basic utensils. Look at the common areas — are they actually usable, or cluttered? Check lighting in hallways and outside the building at dusk. If there's parking, is it secure and well-lit? Take photos or videos during your visit so you can compare options later without relying on memory.

sections.heading: Questions to Ask the Owner or Manager
sections.body: Always confirm these details in writing or over WhatsApp after your visit so you have a record. Ask about the notice period for leaving — is it 15 days, one month, or longer? What's included in the rent: WiFi, water, electricity, laundry? Are there separate charges for any of these? What are the house rules: visiting hours for guests, noise curfew, kitchen access? Are there any hidden deposits, membership fees, or annual charges? Ask about maintenance response time if something breaks — do they fix it same-day or in a week? Confirm the exact move-in date and what happens if you need to move out early. If meals are included, ask to see a sample menu and taste the food if possible. Ask if you can speak to current residents — their honest feedback is worth more than the owner's promises. Get everything in writing before you sign, even if it's just a WhatsApp message.

sections.heading: Safety, Documents, and Practical Steps
sections.body: Before handing over any money, ask for the owner's photo ID and verify it matches. Don't pay cash without a receipt — always get written confirmation of what you've paid and when. Agree on the agreement terms in writing: rent amount, move-in date, house rules, and what happens if either party breaks the agreement. Take photos of the room's condition (empty walls, bed, bathroom) before you move in so damage disputes don't happen later. Register your mobile number with the PG and keep the manager's number saved. If you're coming from out of station, ask if you can do a video tour or arrange a trusted local friend to visit on your behalf and confirm details. Verify nearby police station location and keep emergency numbers handy. On move-in day, do a walk-through with the owner, check all utilities work, and photograph everything again. Trust your instinct — if something feels unsafe or the owner seems evasive, move on even if the room is cheap.

faqs.question: How much advance notice do I need to give before leaving a PG?
faqs.answer: This varies by PG — some ask for 15 days, others a month or more. Always ask this during your visit and confirm it in writing before signing up. It's one of the most common misunderstandings between residents and owners.

faqs.question: What should I do if something is broken in my room?
faqs.answer: Report it to the manager immediately via WhatsApp or in person, and ask for a timeline to fix it. Get their response in writing. If it's urgent (no water, no light), don't wait — escalate the same day. A good PG owner will fix small issues quickly; a bad one will ignore you or delay for months.

faqs.question: Can I have guests or a partner stay over?
faqs.answer: House rules vary widely — some PGs allow it anytime, others limit visiting hours or overnight guests to weekends only. Some charge extra for guests. Ask this question directly and get the answer on WhatsApp so there's no confusion later.

faqs.question: Is it safe to move money over to a PG I've only seen online?
faqs.answer: No. Always visit in person before paying anything, or arrange a trusted friend locally to visit on your behalf and send you photos and video. Never pay full deposits to someone you haven't verified. If something feels rushed or the owner pressures you to decide without visiting, it's usually a red flag.

faqs.question: How do I compare two PGs if I've visited them on different days?
faqs.answer: Take photos and videos at both, write down the questions you asked and answers you got, and note your gut feeling about the owner and other residents. Compare on paper: rent, included utilities, house rules, and location. Sleep on it for a day before deciding. The cheapest option isn't always the best if it means living in a cramped space or dealing with a difficult owner.
